- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or align with 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects downward; adjust downward bias by 1–3% per day of high sentiment.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is volatile; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward recent 10-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 65, model often fails to recognize downward trend; apply downward bias of 3–5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (e.g., bearish signals), model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 5–10% if recent 3-day average is below 65.
